claims.text: In high-entropy-alloy transition-metal catalysts, local lattice distortion combined with grain-boundary elemental segregation enhances catalytic durability under extreme conditions.
Local lattice distortion and grain-boundary segregation modify active-site electronic properties to improve catalytic activity and selectivity.
A sputter-deposited W-Ta-V-Cr refractory HEA can have a single-phase BCC structure with a substantial nanocrystalline grain fraction.
The proposed initial HEA has a random, near-equiatomic distribution of its constituent transition metals.
Relevant refractory HEA systems can contain W, Ta, Cr, and V, with Hf as an additional component.
Magnetron sputtering can produce nanocrystalline W-Ta-Cr-V-based refractory HEA films.
Tailored sputtering, post-deposition annealing, or mild irradiation can promote targeted Cr and V segregation at grain boundaries without causing gross phase separation or precipitation.
The cited refractory HEAs were annealed or irradiated at temperatures around 1073–1173 K.
A nanocrystalline W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEA can undergo annealing at 1173 K with only a small grain-size increase.
The proposed operating and processing conditions ensure a steady-state microstructure without significant grain growth.
Nanocrystalline grain boundaries become enriched in Cr and V.
Cr- and V-enriched grain boundaries intensify local lattice distortion.
Grain-boundary segregation and lattice distortion adjust the d-band center of catalytically active transition-metal sites.
Adjustment of the d-band center optimizes adsorbate binding energies and thereby improves catalytic activity and selectivity.
The proposed electronic modification increases vacancy/interstitial recombination.
Enhanced defect recombination stabilizes catalytic active sites against deactivation.
A W-Ta-V-Cr HEA showed resistance to irradiation-created dislocation loops at 1073 K.
Fine-grained, segregation-engineered HEA catalysts will retain higher activity and selectivity over time than compositionally similar coarse-grained, homogeneous catalysts.
The proposed mechanism applies to refractory HEA catalysts under extreme thermal conditions but may fail when severe phase separation or precipitation dominates.
Prior radiation-resistance or mechanical-behavior evidence supports transferring the lattice-distortion mechanism to catalytic d-band modification.
